headline: Rwanda Cuts Maternal Deaths by 30% in Two Years
meta_description: Rwanda has reduced maternal deaths by 30% in just two years, building on decades of progress powered by digital health innovation.
summary_short: Rwanda has achieved a 30% reduction in maternal deaths in two years, continuing a remarkable 85% decline over the past two decades.
body:
Rwanda has cut maternal deaths by 30% in just two years—a striking milestone that builds on an even more impressive 85% decline over the past 20 years.

The gains rest on a foundation of sustained commitment to maternal health. But what's driving the latest acceleration is technology: digital health systems are now helping community health workers identify high-risk pregnancies early, before complications become life-threatening. This distributed approach brings medical insight to rural areas and remote communities, catching danger signs at a point where intervention can save lives.

The numbers tell a story of how persistent investment in both infrastructure and innovation can reshape outcomes. Rwanda's two-decade journey shows that maternal mortality isn't inevitable—it responds to strategy, resources, and the will to reach every pregnant woman, wherever she lives.
